treatment.logline: In a monsoon-soaked Colombo street, a hungry young vendor and a sheltered woman spark a connection over a lost phone until her father's call breaks the moment, as fate quietly takes note.

arc.feeling: Immersed in rain; Kasun’s quiet drive surfaces
Energy and spark as two worlds brush
A chill cuts through; hope is left hanging
A larger story breathes over a small goodbye

treatment.approach: Grounded realism in heavy rain; kinetic when chance strikes, still when hearts listen. Wide lenses to place them in the city, then longer glass for intimacy. Moves are motivated by pursuit, turns go closer, and rain is a character — on faces, steel, and glass. Sound carries the city; music enters only when connection and destiny rise.

treatment.geography: Screen left: shopfronts and Kasun’s three-wheeler stall under a small awning; screen right: the curb/road where a family car has pulled in. The 180° line runs along the road, with the camera staying stall-side looking toward the curb for the whole scene. OTS singles keep eye-lines consistent; inserts are neutral. We never step across the line.
treatment.key_image: A wet hand lifting a fallen phone from a rain-hammered puddle as the city blurs behind.
advice: We keep the family car near the stall to avoid an unmarked cross-road move; if you prefer it truly across the road, add a [move] beat before the drop.

We shifted the narrator to pure voice-over over picture to comply with the rule that a narrator is only heard; if you want a visible narrator, change L22 to a standard V.O. credit or assign the thought to an on-screen character.
If rain density must be reduced for safety, keep the close-up rain plates (phone, faces) heavy and cheat the wides with sound.
